title: Hybe: GPU-NPU Hybrid System for Efficient LLM Inference with Million-Token Context Window
problem: LLM inference with million-token context windows is infeasible on GPUs alone because KV cache activation memory for long contexts (>100K tokens) exceeds total GPU DRAM capacity, making batching impractical and leaving GPU compute cores severely underutilized during the memory-bandwidth-bound decode stage. The compute-memory imbalance between compute-intensive prefill and memory-intensive decode cannot be addressed by batching when KV data dominates physical memory.
motivation: Context windows are growing toward 1M tokens for long-document reasoning and in-context retrieval, but GPU memory capacity and its fixed compute-to-memory-bandwidth ratio make it an inefficient sole inference platform, creating an opportunity for heterogeneous hardware that matches hardware resources to each stage's bottleneck.
method: Hybe assigns the compute-intensive prefill stage (processing the full context once) to GPUs (NVIDIA H100 with vLLM) and the memory-hungry decode stage (generating tokens one at a time) to lightweight NPUs. The key innovation is fine-grained KV streaming: instead of storing all the key-value cache data (what the model learns about each token in the context) in GPU memory, the GPU streams it directly to the NPU's memory (high-bandwidth memory, or HBM) as it's being computed—this dramatically cuts GPU memory usage. A dynamic scheduler assigns incoming requests to whichever hardware is idle, preventing bottlenecks. The NPU is built in a 4nm process with HBM matching the H100's memory specification.
key_novelty: Streaming key-value cache data piece-by-piece from the GPU to the NPU as it's generated during prefill, rather than storing it all in GPU memory first, enables million-token contexts while keeping the NPU minimally sized for the decode stage.
contributions: Hybe GPU-NPU heterogeneous architecture that separates prefill (GPU) and decode (NPU) inference stages to match hardware to computational characteristics
Fine-grained KV transmission mechanism that streams partial KV activations from GPU to NPU as they are produced, minimizing peak GPU memory pressure
Stage-wise pipeline scheduler that dynamically assigns requests to idle GPU or NPU to minimize stalls
2.1x speedup for 100K-token context (Phi-3) and 3.9x energy efficiency for 1M-token context (Llama-3) versus equal-count H100 GPUs

metrics.speedup: 2.1x for Phi-3 with 100K-token context vs H100 GPU
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 3.9x energy efficiency for Llama-3 with 1M-token context vs equal-count H100 GPUs

baselines: NVIDIA H100 GPU with vLLM (equal device count)
limitations: NPU interconnect bandwidth and the cost/area of deploying paired NPUs alongside existing GPU infrastructure are not quantified.
primary_theme: Heterogeneous GPU-NPU disaggregation for long-context LLM inference
